# Code of conduct

## The short version

Be decent to people. Critique code, not the person who wrote it. Assume the
person you are talking to is competent and acting in good faith until they give
you real reason to think otherwise.

## Our pledge

Everyone participating in this project — contributors, issue reporters,
maintainers — is entitled to a harassment-free experience regardless of age,
body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics,
gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic
status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and
orientation.

## What is expected

- **Give feedback on the work.** "This allocates on every keystroke" is useful.
  "This is amateur code" is not, and says nothing a reviewer can act on.
- **Accept feedback on your work.** Someone finding a bug in your patch is the
  system working, not an attack.
- **Assume competence.** Beginners ask questions that look obvious to you; that
  is what beginners are for. Answer them or stay quiet.
- **Be clear about uncertainty.** "I think, but have not verified" is a
  contribution. Confident wrongness costs everyone time.

## What is not acceptable

- Harassment, insults, or personal or political attacks
- Sexualized language or imagery, and unwelcome sexual attention
- Publishing others' private information without explicit permission
- Sustained disruption of discussions
- Any other conduct reasonably considered inappropriate in a professional setting

## Scope

This applies in all project spaces — issues, pull requests, discussions, commit
messages, code comments — and when representing the project publicly.

## Enforcement

Report conduct issues privately to the maintainer via the address on the
repository's GitHub profile. Reports are handled confidentially. As a
single-maintainer project there is no committee: I read the report, I decide, and
I explain the decision to the person who reported it.

Responses escalate with severity and repetition, from a private correction, to a
public one, to a temporary ban, to a permanent one. Anyone whose contribution is
excellent is not thereby exempt; there is no contributor this project needs
badly enough to tolerate mistreating people for.
